title: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain
title_zh: 人脑中跨语言的共享意义成分
abstract: Human languages differ profoundly in their sounds, words and grammatical systems, yet all support the communication of complex meanings. How the brain handles this diversity remains a fundamental question in language neuroscience. Multilingual neural network models offer a way to answer this question by representing linguistic content across languages in a shared space. Leveraging these advances, we evaluated the similarity of linguistic representations in speakers of 21 languages. Here we combined existing (12 languages across 4 language families) and newly collected functional magnetic resonance imaging data (9 languages across 4 families) to test encoding models predicting brain activity in the language network using representations from multilingual models. Model representations predicted brain responses reliably within each language. Critically, encoding models trained on one set of languages generalized zero-shot to previously unseen languages, accurately predicting neural responses without exposure to the target language. This cross-lingual generalization extended across variation in language family, stimulus type and presentation modality. These findings point to a shared cross-lingual component for meaning across human languages. Using fMRI data from speakers of 21 languages and multilingual language models, de Varda et al. show that brain encoding models trained on some languages predict responses to unseen languages, pointing to a shared meaning component across languages.
abstract_zh: 人类语言在声音、词汇和语法系统上存在深刻差异，但都支持复杂意义的交流。大脑如何处理这种多样性仍然是语言神经科学的一个基本问题。多语言神经网络模型提供了一种解决该问题的方法，即在共享空间中跨语言表示语言内容。利用这些进展，我们评估了21种语言使用者之间的语言表征相似性。在此，我们结合了现有数据（4个语系中的12种语言）和新收集的功能磁共振成像数据（4个语系中的9种语言），测试了使用多语言模型的表征来预测语言网络脑活动的编码模型。模型表征能可靠地预测每种语言中的脑反应。关键的是，在一组语言上训练的编码模型可以零样本推广至此前未见的语言，在不接触目标语言的情况下准确预测神经反应。这种跨语言推广延伸至语系、刺激类型和呈现方式的差异。这些发现表明，人类语言中存在跨语言的共享意义成分。使用21种语言使用者的fMRI数据和多语言语言模型，de Varda等人表明，在某些语言上训练的脑编码模型能预测未见语言的反应，指向跨语言的共享意义成分。
